subject: PII field mapping, data sovereignty & subprocessors — evidence requested
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medsource.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@medsource.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PII mapping + subprocessors — initial questionnaire

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for agreeing to engage on our privacy checklist. We ran through the questionnaire internally and had a few clarifying asks before we mark items as 'satisfied' on our side. Attached is our baseline (MedSource_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx) with the fields we care most about. A few specific asks below:

1) Field-level mapping: Can you provide a simple mapping that shows which input fields Redwood sends to model inference, which fields are persisted (logs, KV cache), and where (region/zone)? We need to map: patient_id, contact_email, free_text_notes, encounter_timestamp.
2) Data residency & export controls: We are EU-based for some customers — what options do you expose to guarantee that inference and any persistent storage stay in EU-only regions?
3) Subprocessors: Please share your current list of subprocessors (full legal names) and whether any third parties have access to unredacted PII.
4) KMS / keys: Do you support customer-managed keys (BYOK) for Private deployments and for Dedicated? How are ephemeral keys handled for hosted API?
5) Logs & telemetry: Are request logs hashed or reversible? Is there a mode to disable retention of request content entirely?

We'd appreciate a short dataflow sketch (even ASCII) that shows the path from ingestion to model to storage. Also please flag any items that would require a contract addendum or a signed attestation.

Goal: we need evidence for our privacy team by EOW (Fri, 2026-08-27). If you need more time let us know. Happy to do a 30-min call.

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Security Architect — MedSource Health
security@medsource.com

Attachments:
 - MedSource_security_questionnaire_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medsource.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 12:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PII mapping + subprocessors — initial questionnaire

Hi Sanjay — thanks, this is helpful. I've started a short mapping and attached a CSV (redwood_pii_field_map_v1.csv) that shows our defaults. High level answers inline below and a couple of asks so we provide the exact evidence you need.

1) Field-level mapping (high level):
 - patient_id: used as a correlation key only. Not included in model input by default for text generation requests unless explicitly passed in the prompt. If present in prompt it will be treated as input and flows to inference (transient).
 - contact_email: considered PII and redacted by default in logs/persistent traces.
 - free_text_notes:  sent to the model for inference. We provide token-level masking options and a field-based preprocessor to strip PHI before forwarding.
 - encounter_timestamp: metadata; stored in request metadata (non-sensitive) and retained according to retention policy.

We can produce a more formal dataflow diagram. Quick ASCII sketch below (will formalize after you confirm which options you need):

[ingest/API gateway] -> [pre-processor: field filters / redaction] -> [inference runtime / KV cache] -> [post-processor: redact/normalize] -> [long-term logs / metrics store]

Notes: KV cache is an in-memory cache persisted to encrypted ephemeral storage for warm-starts. By default keys are encrypted with provider-managed KMS keys; customers on Dedicated/Private can enable BYOK.

2) Data residency: Hosted API routes can be pinned by region (us-west-2, eu-west-1). For EU-only residency and no egress, we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated with region pinning. We can provide a deployment topology document for EU-only options.

3) Subprocessors: We maintain a registry; I'll attach a snapshot and Rishi will follow up with legal wording. In short: cloud infra providers (AWS), monitoring vendors (Datadog — access limited to telemetry), CDN/edge providers (Fastly for hosted edge), and a small set of managed services. No third party has access to unredacted PII for Private deployments unless explicitly enabled.

4) KMS / keys: BYOK supported for Private and Dedicated. For Hosted: we offer customer-supplied encryption keys for stored artifacts under an enterprise addendum; ephemeral inference keys are rotated frequently and managed by Redwood if BYOK is not enabled.

5) Logs & telemetry: Request bodies are hashed for short-term telemetry; hashes are not reversible. We also offer a retention policy setting — default 30 days, can be reduced to 0 (no retention) for enterprise contracts.

Next steps: 
 - I've attached redwood_dpa_summary.pdf (high-level DPA clauses relevant to PII).
 - Rishi (legal) / Evelyn (privacy) are looped to confirm contract language and any addendum.
 - Can you confirm whether you need SOC2 evidence under NDA, and whether you need a signed subprocessors addendum?

If it helps, we can do a tech walkthrough tomorrow (Fri) 10:30am PDT. Would that work for your team?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachments:
 - redwood_pii_field_map_v1.csv (CSV)
 - redwood_dpa_summary.pdf (PDF)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medsource.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: security@medsource.com
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PII mapping + subprocessors — initial questionnaire

Thanks Kimberly — this is exactly the level we were hoping for. A few follow-ups before we schedule the walkthrough:

- On hashes: our privacy team treats stable hashed identifiers as PII if they are used as a persistent link between systems (because they de-anonymize in combination with other data sources). Can you confirm how long hashed identifiers may exist in logs/indices?
- KV cache: is the cache ever written to disk in hosted mode (for crash recovery), or is it always in-memory? You mentioned ephemeral storage — can we get an option that disables any disk persistence for our account?
- Subprocessors: we will likely need a signed subprocessors addendum. Please let us know what you can provide and the expected turnaround.
- Evidence: SOC2 is required, and our procurement will request the report. We'll accept an NDA and redacted report. Please send the access instructions.

One more ask: can Redwood confirm whether the pre-processor rule engine supports configurable regexes and/or regex lookups for PHI patterns (SSNs, MRNs, emails) so we can tune filters client-side?

If you can answer these by EOD Monday (24 Aug) that gives us time to feed into our privacy review. If not, a short call early next week is fine.

Cheers,
Sanjay
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@medsource.com>, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2026 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PII mapping + subprocessors — initial questionnaire

Hi Sanjay — Rishi here from Legal. Quick answers to your follow-ups and what we can deliver next week: 

1) Hashed identifiers: We treat stable hashed IDs as PII when they are persistent and linkable. Default telemetry hashes are short-lived (rotated) and not stored in a globally queryable index for hosted customers. For Dedicated/Private we can provide configuration to avoid long-term indexing. We will provide a short attestation note on hashing practices.

2) KV cache persistence: In hosted mode, the runtime uses an in-memory KV cache and persists to encrypted ephemeral disk only for instance restart recovery; that disk is encrypted with KMS and scrubbed on termination. For MedSource's needs we can:
 - Disable disk persistence for your account (in hosted) so cache remains memory-only (this will trade off cold-start latency).
 - Or provision Dedicated capacity with guaranteed memory-only volatility.

3) Subprocessors addendum & SOC2: We can provide a signed subprocessors addendum. We'll also provide the SOC2 report (redacted) under an NDA and can share instructions to retrieve it via our secure portal. Expected turnaround: 3-5 business days after NDA is in place. I attached a registry snapshot (subprocessors_registry_2026-07.csv) for your immediate review.

4) Pre-processor rule engine: Yes — it supports configurable regex-based rules and pattern libraries (SSN, email, MRN). We also offer a client-side filter library you can run before sending to Redwood if you prefer end-to-end control.

Deliverables we will send by Tue EOD (2026-08-24):
 - Formal dataflow diagram (PDF) scoped to your requested fields.
 - Signed subprocessors addendum draft.
 - Instructions and secure link for redacted SOC2 report.
 - Short attestation on hash handling and retention windows.

If you want, we can keep the Fri 10:30am PDT tech walkthrough as a contingency; otherwise we can plan the call after you've reviewed the artifacts.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com

Attachments:
 - subprocessors_registry_2026-07.csv
 - SOC2-report-redacted.pdf
